record_body:
=== Company summary ===
- AcmeAI (acmeai.com). Building an AI platform layer used by internal product teams + a few external customers.
- Current status: ACTIVE evaluation. Strong interest in Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and/or Private (VPC). Hosted API used for quick prototyping but they expect to land in VPC for production.

=== Ownership / team ===
- AE: Ethan Park
- SE: Nadia Rahman (also supporting cost/latency attribution + workload sizing)
- Eng contacts mentioned: Runtime team (kernel selection) as needed for deep dives; keep comms routed through SE.

=== What they’re building / use cases ===
1) Summarization pipeline
   - Batchy but latency-sensitive on interactive summaries.
2) Support-agent chat (tool calling)
   - Needs stable decode latency under mixed concurrency.
3) Doc-search / embeddings
   - Less urgent for this evaluation but they want a single vendor for both embeddings + generation.
4) Internal code-assistant
   - Long prompts are common (repo context) with occasional very long-context spikes.

=== Key requirements (performance + serving behavior) ===
Performance targets (stated on 2026-02-14 deep dive):
- “We care less about absolute best-case and more about p95 stability.”
- p95 latency guardrails:
  - Short prompts: must be consistently fast (they’re sensitive to regressions that show up as UI jank)
  - Long-context prompts: want predictable p95 even if throughput drops; avoid variance between GPU SKUs
- Throughput: wants a clear tok/s per GPU expectation by model family + prompt bucket.

Sequence length distribution (approx; from call notes, not yet validated via logs):
- Prefill-heavy workload mix. Large prompt variance.
- Buckets they care about:
  - “short”: ~0.5k–2k input tokens (high volume)
  - “medium”: ~4k–8k input tokens
  - “long”: ~16k–32k input tokens (low volume but drives p95 + incident perception)
- Decode lengths: usually 150–800 tokens; occasional 1.5k tokens for summarization.

GPU constraints / fleet reality:
- They expect mixed GPU SKUs for cost reasons:
  - L4 for baseline + scale-out
  - A10 for some existing capacity
  - A100 for peak and long-context workloads
  - Interested in H100 later but not in first phase
- They explicitly asked whether Redwood performance is consistent across L4 vs A10 for long context (they’ve seen “weird p95” elsewhere when mixing SKUs).

Model preferences:
- Open models preferred; they are flexible on exact family but want:
  - long-context capable variants
  - stable kernel/runtime behavior across minor model revs
- They asked whether Redwood can pin model version + have rollback/fallback policies.

Routing / fallback:
- Wants ability to:
  - route long-context traffic to higher-end GPUs automatically
  - have deterministic fallback if capacity constrained (same model family preferred)
- “If you switch a kernel or a model variant under us, we need to know and have a safety valve.”

=== Deployment + security ===
- Deployment: VPC required for production. They may accept Hosted for a short POC if audit logging + retention controls are clear.
- Security checklist items called out:
  - SSO/SAML for console access
  - audit logs (admin + access)
  - KMS integration (customer-managed keys)
  - retention controls / log retention policy
  - data residency: prefer US regions initially; EU later for one business unit

=== Evaluation timeline / recent activity ===
- 2026-01-28: Account created after inbound from performance benchmarks page; requested Dedicated pricing + GPU options.
- 2026-02-03: Discovery call (AE+SE). Primary theme: tail latency variance + long context.
- 2026-02-10: Shared initial sizing assumptions; AcmeAI pushed back on “single SKU” suggestion; they want mixed fleet.
- 2026-02-14: Runtime performance deep dive (Fireflies: ff_2026_02_14_runtime_performance_deep_dive_acmeai).
  - Focus: kernel selection, prefill vs decode regimes, long-context buckets, L4/A10 behavior.
  - Action item: provide a clear plan for validating kernel selection stability + override/rollback during POC.
- 2026-02-18: Follow-up email thread: asked about kernel pinning + “explain why this kernel was chosen” tooling.
- 2026-02-24: SE sent draft POC plan + requested anonymized prompt histogram + concurrency traces.

=== Notes from 2026-02-14 deep dive (high signal excerpts) ===
- “We’ve had incidents where a runtime upgrade changed performance on A10 only; we can’t relive that.”
- “Our prompts have a long tail; the 20k token cases are rare but they define our SLO story.”
- Asked specifically:
  - Do you bucket by effective context length and treat prefill/decode differently?
  - Can we see which kernel got picked (in traces/metrics)?
  - Can we override kernel choice per model family during evaluation?

=== Current evaluation plan (draft) ===
POC success criteria:
- Demonstrate stable p95 for long-context bucket across L4 + A10 + A100 (no unexplained variance; provide instrumentation).
- Provide operator controls:
  - feature-flagged selector behavior
  - deterministic fallback path
  - emergency override/pinning guidance
- Provide benchmark report format they can reuse internally (model family + GPU SKU + seq bucket).

=== Risks / watchouts ===
- Sensitive to regressions that correlate with:
  - new GPU types introduced into cluster
  - new model family onboarded
  - runtime upgrades (esp. kernel selector changes)
- They will likely ask for a “no surprises” change-management story (release notes + guardrails + canary process).

=== Next steps (internal) ===
- Nadia: map AcmeAI seq distribution into Redwood benchmark harness format (needs their histogram/log sample).
- Ethan: send updated Dedicated/VPC pricing band with mixed-SKU assumptions.
- If they move forward with POC: ensure we can demonstrate kernel selection observability and provide a safe rollback story (tie to selector-v2 rollout guardrails).

=== Next steps (external) ===
- Request from AcmeAI:
  - anonymized prompt length histogram (prefill + decode) + concurrency profile
  - preferred model shortlist (or constraints: context length + quality bar)
- Schedule 60-min POC kickoff with their infra lead + security lead.

=== Open questions ===
- Do they require on-prem eventually or is VPC sufficient for 12–18 months?
- Are they OK with separate pools for long-context vs general traffic (routing policy), or must it be one shared pool?
- Who is final signer: platform eng vs procurement (unclear; they mentioned “security will gate everything”).
